fields.quoted_span:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses.
fields.note: Source-of-income prohibition, Section 8 example, protected classes, 180-day/2-year filing windows are supported. Not found in D068: the landlord may still refuse for insufficient income or poor credit, and the fines up to $10,000 for a first offense.

fields.quoted_span:
You may file a complaint with us for free within 180 days
of the date of the alleged violation.
fields.note: The 180-day DCR window and the two-year Superior Court window are supported ("within two years of the alleged violation"). The $10,000 first-offense fine is not stated in the document.
The field is empty and the document gives no effective date for the source-of-income provision. The brochure revision date (06.18.15) is not an effective date.

fields.quoted_span:
The Division on Civil Rights enforces the New Jersey
Law Against Discrimination.
fields.note: The brochure describes the LAD as currently enforced, which is consistent with in_force, but it does not state a status explicitly. It is dated 2015.

fields.quoted_span:
The provisions of the LAD apply to the sale or rental of all
property including open land, whether for business or
residential purposes, with the following exceptions:
fields.note: The two owner-occupancy exemptions, the religious preference exemption and the older-persons familial-status exemption are all in the document. The single-sex residence exemption is not in D068 but appears in coverage evidence from D067.

fields.quoted_span: (as defined in the LAD at N.J.S.A. 10:5-5mm)
fields.note: D068 cites only N.J.S.A. 10:5-5mm, for the older persons definition. It does not give N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) or the other listed citations. The rule's review note says the section cite comes from the DCA guide.
